name: Johnson-noise thermometer
summary: A primary thermometer from a resistor's own noise. Every stage is on paper; nothing is built or bought.

assumptions.assumption: the resistor is in thermal equilibrium at one temperature
assumptions.how_checked: two readings 10 minutes apart agree within the statistical interval
assumptions.if_broken: the reading is a weighted average of gradients; flag UNCAL

assumptions.assumption: Re Z is known across the band (pure R, or R with a known shunt C)
assumptions.how_checked: measure Re Z(f) with the injected-tone sweep before each run
assumptions.if_broken: band-edge bias; at 100 kOhm and 100 pF, Re Z falls 28 percent by 10 kHz
assumptions.door: measure Re Z(f) in place with the injected sweep and divide it out, or lower R and C so the droop is negligible

assumptions.assumption: no excess (1/f or current) noise in the resistor
assumptions.how_checked: metal-film part, no DC bias, and the PSD is flat across 1 to 10 kHz within its interval
assumptions.if_broken: T reads high; drop the band or the part
assumptions.door: fit a 1/f term, or raise the band floor

assumptions.assumption: classical limit, h f << kB T
assumptions.how_checked: kB T / h is 6.2 THz at 300 K, 9 orders above the band

assumptions.assumption: the two amplifier chains' noises are uncorrelated
assumptions.how_checked: zero-correlation null: independent noise into each chain must cross-correlate to zero (new check zeronull)
assumptions.if_broken: correlated amplifier noise reads as temperature; shield, separate grounds and supplies
assumptions.door: measure the correlated floor with the zero-correlation null and subtract it

assumptions.assumption: no interference couples into both chains
assumptions.how_checked: shorted-input cross spectrum (auto-zero) is flat and below 1e-4 of the signal
assumptions.if_broken: mains and radio lines read as heat; reject lines, improve the shield
assumptions.door: subtract the shorted-input cross spectrum, or reject the lines
